new_quiz.q: What does the Water plugin add to Unreal Engine?
choices: A tool that paints wet materials on meshes
Ready-made lakes, rivers and oceans you can place in a level
A weather system with rain and snow
A sound library with water effects
new_quiz.explain: The Water plugin gives you water bodies such as lakes, rivers and oceans. You place them in a level like other actors.

new_quiz.q: Where do you enable the Water plugin?
choices: In Landscape Mode, on the Manage tab
In the Details panel of the Landscape
In the Place Actors panel, under Volumes
In Edit, then Plugins, by searching for Water
new_quiz.explain: You open Edit, then Plugins, search for Water and enable the Water plugin. The editor must restart before the plugin works.

new_quiz.q: You enabled the Water plugin, but you cannot find a Water Body in the Place Actors panel. What do you check first?
choices: That you restarted the editor after enabling the plugin
That the level has a Directional Light
That the project uses the Third Person template
That the Landscape has a material
new_quiz.explain: A newly enabled plugin only loads after the editor restarts. Until then its actors, such as Water Body Lake, are not available.

new_quiz.q: What controls the outline of a Water Body Lake or a Water Body River?
choices: A texture painted on the Landscape
The scale of a cube volume
A spline with points you can move
The size of the Water plugin window
new_quiz.explain: A water body is shaped by a spline, which is a line with points. You select the water, then click and move its points to change the outline.

new_quiz.q: Why is water a useful edge in level design?
choices: It makes the level load faster
It shows the player where the route ends without a wall
It stops the player from jumping
It removes the need for lighting
new_quiz.explain: Players read a shore as a natural limit. The water marks the end of the route, so you do not need a wall there.

new_quiz.q: How should the path relate to the water in your level?
choices: The path should end in the middle of the water
The path should be hidden under the water
The path should cross the water many times
The path should run beside the water
new_quiz.explain: The water is used as a boundary that the path runs beside. It should guide the player, and not be a blocker that the player cannot understand.

new_quiz.q: What is Volumetric Fog?
choices: Fog that reacts to light in 3D
Fog that is painted on a flat texture
Fog that only appears in Play mode
Fog that is made of small meshes
new_quiz.explain: Volumetric Fog is calculated in 3D space, so lights can light it and cast shadows through it. That is why it gives more mood than simple distance fog.

new_quiz.q: Where do you turn on Volumetric Fog?
choices: In the Details panel of the Directional Light
In the settings of the Place Actors panel
In the Details panel of the Exponential Height Fog actor
In the view mode menu of the viewport
new_quiz.explain: Volumetric Fog is an option of the Exponential Height Fog actor. You select that actor in the Outliner and turn the option on in the Details panel.

new_quiz.q: What is a Local Fog Volume?
choices: A volume that removes fog from a room
A small area of fog that you place in the level
A setting that changes the fog of the whole level
A light that only shines through fog
new_quiz.explain: A Local Fog Volume is a placeable actor that holds fog in one small area. It lets you add fog in one spot without changing the rest of the level.

new_quiz.q: Why do you place thick fog over a dead end?
choices: Fog blocks the player like a wall
Fog makes the dead end load faster
Fog hides mistakes in the blockout
Foggy places feel less inviting, so players go toward the clear areas
new_quiz.explain: Fog does not stop the player, but it changes how a place feels. Players tend to move toward clear areas, so the fog guides them away from the dead end.

new_quiz.q: What happens when you raise the two Extinction values of a Local Fog Volume?
choices: The fog becomes thicker
The fog changes colour
The fog volume becomes larger
The fog moves upward
new_quiz.explain: The Extinction values control how dense the fog is. Higher values make the fog thicker, so less can be seen through it.

new_quiz.q: After you add the fog, what must you still be able to see clearly?
choices: The floor of the dead end
The Exponential Height Fog actor
The goal and the landmark
The edges of the Local Fog Volume
new_quiz.explain: The fog should make one dead end less inviting, and nothing more. If it hides the goal or the landmark, the player loses the things that guide them.

new_quiz.q: What is a decal?
choices: A light that shines in one direction
A mesh with a very low number of triangles
A material that is projected onto surfaces
A volume that blocks the player
new_quiz.explain: A decal is a material projected onto the surfaces it touches, like a sticker, a stain or a painted arrow. It adds detail without changing the mesh below it.

new_quiz.q: Which Material Domain do you set for a material that a Decal Actor can use?
choices: Surface
Deferred Decal
Post Process
User Interface
new_quiz.explain: A decal material needs its Material Domain set to Deferred Decal. In this quest you also set its Blend Mode to Translucent.

new_quiz.q: Where do you choose the material that a Decal Actor shows?
choices: In the Decal Material property in its Details panel
In the Place Actors panel, before you drag it in
In the view mode menu of the viewport
In the material of the floor below it
new_quiz.explain: You select the Decal Actor and set Decal Material in the Details panel. The surface below keeps its own material.

new_quiz.q: You placed a Decal Actor but you cannot see the decal. What do you check first?
choices: That the level has a Sky Light
That the floor mesh has collision
That the project was saved
That the box of the decal touches a surface
new_quiz.explain: A decal only shows where its box touches a surface. Rotate and move the Decal Actor until the box reaches the floor or the wall.

new_quiz.q: How can a few decals on the ground guide the player?
choices: They push the character in one direction
They form a line that leads the eye toward a route
They light the route like lamps
They block the other routes
new_quiz.explain: A trail of scuffs, arrows or stains leads the eye of the player toward a route entrance. It works without any text or sign.

new_quiz.q: What is a fast way to copy a decal that is already in the level?
choices: Press G while it is selected
Press F while it is selected
Hold Alt and drag it
Hold Ctrl and click it
new_quiz.explain: Holding Alt while you drag an actor makes a copy and moves the copy. This is a quick way to lay out three or four decals in a line.

new_quiz.q: What is a Level Instance?
choices: A backup copy of the whole project
A single mesh that replaces a room
A camera bookmark saved in a level
A group of actors saved as its own small level that you can place many times
new_quiz.explain: A Level Instance stores a group of actors as a small level. You can then place that level many times inside a bigger level.

new_quiz.q: How do you turn a selected room into a Level Instance?
choices: Right-click the selection, open Level and choose Create Level Instance
Drag the selection into the Content Browser
Press Ctrl+G to group the selection
Open File and choose Save Current Level As
new_quiz.explain: You select all the actors of the room, right-click, open Level and choose Create Level Instance. A window opens and then you save the new level file.

new_quiz.q: You have three copies of a Level Instance. What happens when you edit one copy and commit the change?
choices: Only that copy changes
All three copies change
The other two copies are deleted
A fourth copy is created
new_quiz.explain: All copies point to the same level file. A change that you commit in one copy shows up in every copy.

new_quiz.q: How do you start editing one copy of a Level Instance?
choices: Double-click it in the Content Browser while Play is running
Delete it and build the room again
Select it and click Edit in the Details panel
Select it and press F on the keyboard
new_quiz.explain: You select one copy and click Edit in the Details panel. The actors inside can then be moved and changed.

new_quiz.q: You moved a wall while editing a Level Instance. How do you finish the edit so that the change is saved to all copies?
choices: Press Play and stop again
Select the Level Instance in the Outliner and click Commit Changes
Hold Alt and drag the instance
Right-click the wall and choose Create Level Instance
new_quiz.explain: Commit Changes in the Details panel ends the edit and saves the level file of the instance. After that, every copy shows the moved wall.

new_quiz.q: When does a Level Instance save the most work?
choices: When a level uses the same room or building several times
When a level has only one room
When every room in a level must look different
When a level has no actors yet
new_quiz.explain: With a Level Instance you build and fix the room once. Every place that uses it gets the same change, so you do not repeat the work.

new_quiz.q: What is a landscape spline?
choices: A brush that paints grass on a landscape
A curved line that you draw on a landscape with control points
A wall that marks the edge of a landscape
A copy of a landscape at a lower resolution
new_quiz.explain: A landscape spline is a curved line made of control points. Unreal can shape the ground to follow it, which is a fast way to make roads and paths.

new_quiz.q: Where do you find the Splines tool?
choices: In the Place Actors panel, under Shapes
In the Details panel of the Landscape
In Modeling Mode, under Create
In Landscape Mode, on the Manage tab
new_quiz.explain: You switch to Landscape Mode, open the Manage tab and select the Splines tool there.

new_quiz.q: How do you place the control points of a landscape spline?
choices: Hold Ctrl and click on the landscape
Hold Alt and press G
Double-click on the Outliner
Press F on each spot
new_quiz.explain: With the Splines tool active, you hold Ctrl and click on the landscape. Each new click adds a control point that is joined to the last one.

new_quiz.q: What happens when you deform the landscape to the spline?
choices: The spline is deleted from the level
The spline is turned into a static mesh
The ground is shaped to follow the spline
The landscape material is replaced
new_quiz.explain: Unreal raises or lowers the ground along the spline. The path then sits flat on the hill and is easy to walk.

new_quiz.q: After the deform, the path up the hill is too narrow to walk on. What do you do?
choices: Delete the hill and sculpt a new one
Scale the whole Landscape actor up
Add a second spline next to the first
Make the control points wider in the Details panel, then deform again
new_quiz.explain: The width of the path comes from the control points. You select them, raise their width in the Details panel, and run the deform again.

new_quiz.q: Why do you also send a Play in Editor screenshot of you walking on the path?
choices: It shows the control points of the spline
It shows that the path is flat enough to walk
It shows the settings of the Splines tool
It shows the landscape from above
new_quiz.explain: A path can look fine from above and still be too steep or too narrow. Walking on it in the running game is the real test.

new_quiz.q: What does PCG stand for?
choices: Physical Collision Geometry
Player Camera Guide
Procedural Content Generation
Project Content Group
new_quiz.explain: PCG means Procedural Content Generation. You build a graph of rules, and the graph places many objects for you.

new_quiz.q: What does a PCG Graph asset hold?
choices: The rules that decide where objects are placed
The textures of the landscape
The collision of the rock mesh
The camera bookmarks of the level
new_quiz.explain: The graph holds the rules. In this quest the rules read the landscape, pick points on its surface and spawn a mesh on each point.

new_quiz.q: What is the PCG Volume for?
choices: It sets how loud the level is
It stores the rock mesh
It blocks the player from the path
It is the box that marks where the graph works
new_quiz.explain: The PCG Volume marks the area in which the graph places objects. You set Graph on its PCG component so it knows which rules to run.

new_quiz.q: In which order do you connect the three nodes of the scatter graph?
choices: Static Mesh Spawner, Surface Sampler, Get Landscape Data
Get Landscape Data, Surface Sampler, Static Mesh Spawner
Surface Sampler, Static Mesh Spawner, Get Landscape Data
Surface Sampler, Get Landscape Data, Static Mesh Spawner
new_quiz.explain: First the graph reads the landscape, then it samples points on that surface, and last it spawns a mesh on each point.

new_quiz.q: Where do you choose which rock mesh the graph places?
choices: Under Mesh Entries in the Static Mesh Spawner node
Under Graph on the PCG component
Under Plugins in the Edit menu
Under Manage in Landscape Mode
new_quiz.explain: The Static Mesh Spawner node has a list named Mesh Entries. You add one entry and pick the rock mesh there.

new_quiz.q: The scattered rocks block the path. How do you fix this in this quest?
choices: Delete each rock by hand
Turn off the PCG plugin
Move the PCG Volume away from the path
Make the rock mesh smaller
new_quiz.explain: Rocks only appear inside the volume. If the volume does not cover the path, no rocks are placed on it.

new_quiz.q: Which actor acts as the sun in a level?
choices: The Sky Light
The Point Light
The Post Process Volume
The Directional Light
new_quiz.explain: The Directional Light lights the whole level from one direction, like the sun. For the night copy you turn it into moonlight.

new_quiz.q: How do you make the Directional Light read as moonlight?
choices: Raise its Intensity and set a warm orange Light Color
Rotate it low, lower its Intensity and set a cool blue Light Color
Delete it and add many Spot Lights
Move it far away from the level
new_quiz.explain: A low angle, a dim Intensity and a cool blue Light Color together read as moonlight. Moving a Directional Light does not change its light, only rotating it does.

new_quiz.q: Why do you lock the exposure in the night level?
choices: So the picture does not brighten by itself
So the lights cast no shadows
So the level loads faster
So the sun cannot be rotated
new_quiz.explain: With automatic exposure the camera brightens a dark picture, and the night looks like a grey day. Locking the exposure keeps the level as dim as you set it.

new_quiz.q: How do you lock the exposure for the whole level?
choices: Set Intensity to 0 on the Directional Light
Turn on Volumetric Fog on the Exponential Height Fog
Add a Post Process Volume, tick Infinite Extent (Unbound) and set Metering Mode to Manual
Switch the view mode of the viewport to Unlit
new_quiz.explain: Metering Mode is in the Exposure section of the Post Process Volume. Infinite Extent (Unbound) makes the volume affect the whole level, not only the inside of its box.

new_quiz.q: What must the player still be able to see in the night level?
choices: Every route entrance and the goal
Every wall and every cube
The Directional Light actor
The sky and the horizon
new_quiz.explain: The same rules apply at night as in daylight. The player must see where the routes begin and where the goal is.

new_quiz.q: Which lights do you add to keep the night level readable?
choices: A second Directional Light
A brighter Sky Light
A larger Post Process Volume
Local lights such as Point Lights and Spot Lights
new_quiz.explain: Local lights light only a small area. Placed at the route entrances and the goal, they mark these spots while the rest of the level stays dark.

new_quiz.q: What does attenuation control for a sound?
choices: How fast the sound plays
How the sound gets quieter with distance
How many times the sound repeats
How the sound echoes in a room
new_quiz.explain: Attenuation sets how the volume of a sound falls as the listener moves away. It decides how far the sound reaches.

new_quiz.q: What is created when you drag a sound from the Content Browser into the level?
choices: An Audio Volume
A Reverb Effect
An Ambient Sound actor
A Sound Cue asset
new_quiz.explain: Dragging a sound into the level creates an Ambient Sound actor at that spot. The actor plays the sound from its position in the level.

new_quiz.q: How does a sound near the goal pull the player toward it?
choices: It gets louder as the player gets closer
It gets quieter as the player gets closer
It stops when the player moves
It plays only at the start of the level
new_quiz.explain: A sound that grows louder tells the player they are moving toward its source. This guides the player without anything on screen.

new_quiz.q: Where do you set how far the sound of an Ambient Sound actor reaches?
choices: In the Place Actors panel, under Volumes
In the Settings menu of the Content Browser
In the Reverb section of an Audio Volume
In the Details panel, under Attenuation, after you turn on Override Attenuation
new_quiz.explain: Override Attenuation lets you set the values on the actor itself. Inner Radius and Falloff Distance then decide where the sound is loud and how far it fades out.

new_quiz.q: Which actor do you place around a room to change its reverb?
choices: A Post Process Volume
An Audio Volume
An Ambient Sound actor
A Local Fog Volume
new_quiz.explain: An Audio Volume changes how sound behaves inside it. Under Reverb you turn on Apply Reverb and pick a Reverb Effect.

new_quiz.q: You want to use the engine sound WhiteNoise, but you cannot find it in the Content Browser. What do you turn on?
choices: Override Attenuation in the Details panel
Apply Reverb in the Audio Volume
Show Engine Content in the Settings menu of the Content Browser
Looping in the sound asset
new_quiz.explain: Engine content is hidden by default. Show Engine Content makes the engine folders visible, and WhiteNoise is one of the engine sounds.

new_quiz.q: What is a Landscape Grass Type?
choices: A brush that sculpts hills on a landscape
A texture that colours the ground green
A volume that marks where the player can walk
An asset that lets the landscape material place grass by itself
new_quiz.explain: A Landscape Grass Type holds the grass mesh and its settings. The landscape material uses it to place grass on the layers you choose.

new_quiz.q: Which node connects the Landscape Grass Type to the Landscape Material?
choices: Landscape Grass Output
Static Mesh Spawner
Surface Sampler
Texture Sample
new_quiz.explain: You add a Landscape Grass Output node in the Landscape Material and set the Landscape Grass Type on it. The material then tells the landscape where the grass grows.

new_quiz.q: What do you add to the Landscape Grass Type asset so that it has something to place?
choices: A landscape spline
A grass mesh
A decal material
A PCG Graph
new_quiz.explain: The asset needs a grass mesh. The landscape then places many copies of that mesh.

new_quiz.q: Where does the grass grow on the landscape?
choices: Everywhere on the landscape at all times
Only where the ground is flat
Only where its own layer is painted
Only inside a PCG Volume
new_quiz.explain: The grass is tied to a layer of the landscape material. It only grows where that layer is painted.

new_quiz.q: How do you keep the path free of grass?
choices: Paint another layer, such as dirt, along the route
Delete the grass meshes one by one
Lower the landscape under the route
Hide the Landscape Grass Type asset
new_quiz.explain: Painting another layer along the route replaces the grass layer there. With no grass layer, no grass is placed on the path.

new_quiz.q: Why is a clear path through the grass useful for the player?
choices: It makes the grass grow faster
It lets the level use fewer materials
It stops the player from leaving the level
It shows where the route is
new_quiz.explain: A strip of ground with no grass stands out between the grass on both sides. The player reads it as the way to go.

new_quiz.q: What is a silhouette?
choices: The colour of an object in bright light
The shadow an object casts on the floor
The outline of an object seen as one dark shape
The number of triangles in a mesh
new_quiz.explain: A silhouette is the outline you see when the object is one dark shape, for example against the sky.

new_quiz.q: Why does a good landmark need a silhouette that is easy to recognize?
choices: From far away, fine detail disappears and only the outline is left
From far away, colours become stronger
Landmarks are not allowed to have materials
A simple outline makes the mesh load faster
new_quiz.explain: At a distance the player cannot see small details. The outline is what they recognize, so it must be clear.

new_quiz.q: Why do you switch the viewport from Lit to Unlit or Lighting Only for this study?
choices: So the landmarks cast longer shadows
So you judge only the shape
So the sky becomes darker
So the editor runs faster
new_quiz.explain: These view modes remove the effect of materials or of lighting. Nothing then distracts you from the shape of each landmark.

new_quiz.q: Where do you change the view mode?
choices: In the Details panel of the landmark
In the mode dropdown in the main toolbar
In the Place Actors panel
In the view mode menu of the viewport, which shows Lit by default
new_quiz.explain: The view mode menu is in the viewport and shows the name of the current mode, which is Lit by default.

new_quiz.q: Modeling is not in the mode dropdown of the main toolbar. What do you do?
choices: Create a new project from another template
Enable the Modeling Tools Editor Mode plugin in Edit, then Plugins
Switch the viewport to Lighting Only
Open Landscape Mode and choose New
new_quiz.explain: Modeling Mode comes from a plugin. When the plugin is enabled, Modeling appears in the mode dropdown.

new_quiz.q: Which of your three landmark options do you keep?
choices: The one you recognize the fastest
The one that took the longest to build
The one with the most shapes
The one that is the tallest
new_quiz.explain: A landmark works when the player knows it at a glance. You keep the one you recognize the fastest and note why.
